items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: They say that Bolden was such a great hero.

ctx.x: No, before that. You see, he got his drums when they broke down the Cotton Exposition. He got his first real set of drums, but he had kids that he would play on toy instruments before that. He was born in 1873. So the thing that interested me and the early white bands that I hear about, I wonder what kind of social class they came from. Musicians, you're talking

about playing at the opera, would they be accepted? Yes, they were even very much respected, the musicians in the opera. Now, social class... You see, there wasn't such a strong distinction between the classical musicians. The musician who played in the French opera also played for dancing. Sometimes the whole French opera orchestra played for a really fine, fine gala dance. But more often, they went out as leaders of very smaller groups in all of these dance halls. One time there were always an enormous number…

I can imagine that the status of a musician didn't drop too far. But still, it wasn't so much frowning upon it socially. I wouldn't want to leave that impression. When the white male of a New Orleans family didn't learn music, I think it was just simply that this wasn't a good enough perfection financially. There was more money to be made in a whole lot of other things than there was to be made in music as a career.
